policy_title: Implement a New Deal for Working People
stated: Labour will implement 'Labour’s Plan to Make Work Pay: Delivering a New Deal for Working People' within 100 days. This includes banning exploitative zero-hours contracts, ending fire and rehire, introducing day-one basic rights (parental leave, sick pay, protection from unfair dismissal), strengthening workers' collective voice, and creating a Single Enforcement Body for employment rights. They will also make the minimum wage a genuine living wage, accounting for the cost of living, and remove discriminatory age bands.

source.quote: Labour will stop the chaos and turn the page to create a partnership between business and trade unions, by implementing ‘Labour’s Plan to Make Work Pay: Delivering a New Deal for Working People’ in full – introducing legislation within 100 days. This will include banning exploitative zero hours contracts; ending fire and rehire; and introducing basic rights from day one to parental leave, sick pay, and protection from unfair dismissal. We will strengthen the collective voice of workers, including through their trade unions, and create a Single Enforcement Body to ensure employment rights are upheld. Labour will also make sure the minimum wage is a genuine living wage. We will change the remit of the independent Low Pay Commission so for the first time it accounts for the cost of living. Labour will also remove the discriminatory age bands, so all adults are entitled to the same minimum wage, delivering a pay rise to hundreds of thousands of workers across the UK.

bearing_set.reason: The policy directly addresses pay levels (minimum wage as genuine living wage), job security (zero-hours ban, fire-and-rehire prohibition), and employment rights (day-one sick pay, parental leave, unfair dismissal protection) — the core of good work and fair pay.

Raising the minimum wage to a genuine living wage explicitly tied to cost of living, and removing discriminatory age bands, materially affects real disposable income for lower-wage and younger workers — a direct effect on affordability of essentials.

A higher, cost-of-living-indexed minimum wage with uniform age bands is mechanistically redistributive: the income gain is concentrated at the bottom of the wage distribution, narrowing the Gini and the gap between top and bottom.

Employment-rights packages carry a genuinely contested aggregate effect: tighter hiring/firing rules and higher wage floors can reduce firm formation and business investment (worsening), but efficiency-wage and demand-stimulus effects can raise productivity (improving) — the direction is non-negligible and disputed among credible economists, earning a real contested verdict on aggregate living standards and business dynamism.

membership_note: Four fundamentals bear on this policy: O4 (the primary designed-for outcome), O2 (minimum-wage mechanism directly moves cost-of-living affordability), O14 (bottom-heavy distributional incidence narrows the income gap), and O13 (contested aggregate productivity/investment effect). No credible direct mechanism reaches O3, O5–O12, O15 at a non-negligible level.
